title: Contemporary OB/GYN: Why Carrier Screening Should Start Before Pregnancy
summary: Leslie Saltzman, D.O., vice president of consumer health solutions and medical discipline director at Labcorp, writes in Contemporary OB/GYN that carrier screening should become a routine part of preconception preventive care rather than waiting until pregnancy.
body_markdown:
Leslie Saltzman, D.O., vice president of consumer health solutions and medical discipline director at Labcorp, writes in[Contemporary OB/GYN](https://www.contemporaryobgyn.net/view/before-pregnancy-begins-why-the-timing-of-carrier-screening-matters) that carrier screening should become a routine part of preconception preventive care rather than waiting until pregnancy.


**Why it matters:** Screening before conception gives patients more time for partner testing, reproductive planning and informed decision-making, without the time pressures of an ongoing pregnancy.


**By the numbers:** About 80% of infants born with cystic fibrosis have no known family history of the condition, highlighting the limitations of relying on family history alone to identify at-risk pregnancies.


**What they’re saying:** Both the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) recommend carrier screening ideally before conception, but adoption remains inconsistent. Expanded carrier screening can identify genetic risks across diverse populations, including many individuals who are asymptomatic and unaware they are carriers.


**The bottom line:** Moving carrier screening into routine preventive care shifts reproductive health planning from reactive to proactive, helping patients understand their options earlier and make informed decisions before pregnancy begins.


**Read more:**[Before Pregnancy Begins: Why the Timing of Carrier Screening Matters](https://www.contemporaryobgyn.net/view/before-pregnancy-begins-why-the-timing-of-carrier-screening-matters) ( *Contemporary OB/GYN* )
